content.text: See also
http://www.mail-archive.com/fedora-commons-users@lists.sourceforge.net/msg02643.html
This suggests that the default namespace is only missing on FeSL (perhaps some XML processing that's not namespace-aware?)
Steve, can you post the listDatastreams response you're seeing?
I just tested this via the REST-API and the following output I get on a test object does include the FedoraAccessNamespace as the default namespace:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><objectDatastreams  xmlns="
http://www.fedora.info/definitions/1/0/access/
"  xmlns:xsi="
http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance
"  xsi:schemaLocation="
http://www.fedora.info/definitions/1/0/access/
http://www.fedora-commons.org/definitions/1/0/listDatastreams.xsd
" pid="test-rest:1"  baseURL="
http://localhost:8080/fedora/
" >    <datastream dsid="DC" label="Dublin Core Record for this object" mimeType="text/xml" />    <datastream dsid="testListDatastreams" label="" mimeType="text/xml" /></objectDatastreams>
Seems to be only related to FeSL - see the linked thread (and I had FeSL AuthZ turned on when I found this).
Currently seeing if I can implement schema validation for all TestRESTAPI responses (that return XML) so we catch anything like this in the future
Schema validation reveals the following (added as sub-tasks of
getObjectHistory - response has xsi:schemaLocation="
http://www.fedora.info/definitions/1/0/access/
http://www.fedora.info/definitions/1/0/objectHistory.xsd
" but the schema file is fedoraObjectHistory.xsd (404 from the given location) : schema location in response needs correcting or the xsd file needs renaming

datastream profile with asOfDateTIme - cvc-complex-type.3.2.2: Attribute 'dateTime' is not allowed to appear in element 'datastreamProfile' : schema needs updating to allow this (optional) attribute OR don't have the attribute in the response
findObjects/resumeFindObjects do not seem to have schema - they should, so we can avoid unintentionally breaking the API response
validation - does not specify schema in response (there is one at
http://www.fedora.info/definitions/1/0/validation.xsd)
And back to the original issue...
Looks like org.fcrepo.server.security.xacml.pep.rest.objectshandlers.ListDatastreams.filterXML(...)
This is using a javax.xml.parsers.DocumentBuilderFactory which has not been set to be namespace-aware.
Potentially could affect other classes in org.fcrepo.server.security.xacml.pep.rest.objectshandlers
Update: this was the issue.  Fixed, plus one other instance in objecthandlers.
datastreamProfile schema in the source tree does include dateTime attribute. It's the copy on the web server that's out of date. Looks like it was never updated after
Thought we had caught all of these.
/objects/{pid} - getObjectProfile - is in a default namespace
http://www.fedora.info/definitions/1/0/access/
/objects/{pid}/datastreams - listDatastreams - has no namespace
I haven't checked if these two responses are schema-valid.

comments.body:
See also http://www.mail-archive.com/fedora-commons-users@lists.sourceforge.net/msg02643.html

This suggests that the default namespace is only missing on FeSL (perhaps some XML processing that's not namespace-aware?)

Steve, can you post the listDatastreams response you're seeing?

I just tested this via the REST-API and the following output I get on a test object does include the FedoraAccessNamespace as the default namespace:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><objectDatastreams xmlns="http://www.fedora.info/definitions/1/0/access/" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.fedora.info/definitions/1/0/access/ http://www.fedora-commons.org/definitions/1/0/listDatastreams.xsd" pid="test-rest:1" baseURL="http://localhost:8080/fedora/" > <datastream dsid="DC" label="Dublin Core Record for this object" mimeType="text/xml" /> <datastream dsid="testListDatastreams" label="" mimeType="text/xml" /></objectDatastreams>

Seems to be only related to FeSL - see the linked thread (and I had FeSL AuthZ turned on when I found this).

Currently seeing if I can implement schema validation for all TestRESTAPI responses (that return XML) so we catch anything like this in the future

Schema validation reveals the following (added as sub-tasks of FCREPO-713 Closed ):

  • getObjectHistory - response has xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.fedora.info/definitions/1/0/access/ http://www.fedora.info/definitions/1/0/objectHistory.xsd" but the schema file is fedoraObjectHistory.xsd (404 from the given location) : schema location in response needs correcting or the xsd file needs renaming
  • datastream profile with asOfDateTIme - cvc-complex-type.3.2.2: Attribute 'dateTime' is not allowed to appear in element 'datastreamProfile' : schema needs updating to allow this (optional) attribute OR don't have the attribute in the response
  • findObjects/resumeFindObjects do not seem to have schema - they should, so we can avoid unintentionally breaking the API response
  • validation - does not specify schema in response (there is one at http://www.fedora.info/definitions/1/0/validation.xsd)

And back to the original issue...

Looks like org.fcrepo.server.security.xacml.pep.rest.objectshandlers.ListDatastreams.filterXML(...)

This is using a javax.xml.parsers.DocumentBuilderFactory which has not been set to be namespace-aware.

Potentially could affect other classes in org.fcrepo.server.security.xacml.pep.rest.objectshandlers

Update: this was the issue. Fixed, plus one other instance in objecthandlers.
datastreamProfile schema in the source tree does include dateTime attribute. It's the copy on the web server that's out of date. Looks like it was never updated after FCREPO-612 Closed
